questions.q: is 9 actually the ceiling for the level number, and what do I get if I don't pick one at all?
questions.why: Compression is a newtype over u32 with const new/none/fast/best and an impl Default returning Compression(6); the miniz_oxide backend's make() asserts level <= 10 and notes that backend uniquely has a level 10.

questions.q: which byte offsets does the encoder fill in for the 10-byte preamble, and where do the OS byte and that speed/size hint byte come from?
questions.why: GzBuilder::into_header builds vec![0u8; 10], sets 0x1f/0x8b/8/flg/mtime, header[8] = 2/4/0 by level, header[9] = os or 255.

questions.q: I want to stamp the original file name onto the output - is there anything that will blow up if the name has an embedded zero?
questions.why: GzBuilder::filename and comment wrap the bytes in CString::new(...).unwrap(), documented as panicking on a zero byte.

questions.q: my input arrives in tiny chunks and the metadata block spans several of them - how does it pick up where it left off?
questions.why: GzHeaderParser holds a GzHeaderState enum (Start/Xlen/Extra/Filename/Comment/Crc/Complete) whose parse() loop resumes from the stored state and byte counts.

questions.q: a hostile file could claim a gigantic name string - is there a bound on how much gets buffered before erroring?
questions.why: MAX_HEADER_BUF = 65535 and read_to_nul returns InvalidInput "gzip header field too long" once the buffer hits it.

questions.q: if some flag bits nobody uses are turned on in the metadata, does it warn or refuse?
questions.why: FRESERVED masks bits 5-7 and GzHeaderState::Start returns bad_header() when flags & FRESERVED != 0.

questions.q: where does it compare the trailing checksum and byte count against what it actually produced, when I'm pushing compressed bytes into a writer?
questions.why: GzDecoder::finish_and_check_crc reassembles the 8 trailer bytes and returns corrupt() if either the sum or the amount mismatches.

questions.q: the last 8 bytes of the stream turn up in the same write call as the tail of the compressed data - how are they peeled off?
questions.why: GzDecoder::write checks status == Status::StreamEnd && n < buf.len() and extends self.crc_bytes up to CRC_BYTES_LEN from the leftover slice.

questions.q: when concatenated members are being decoded, how does it work out that another one follows instead of stopping?
questions.why: bufread GzDecoder's Finished arm peeks with fill_buf().is_empty(), resets the crc and inflate state and goes back to Header; the write-side MultiGzDecoder sees Ok(0) and rebuilds a fresh GzDecoder over the taken writer.

questions.q: after pulling out everything, can I still get at whatever bytes followed the compressed blob?
questions.why: Both decoders park in an End state returning Ok(0) and expose into_inner()/get_mut() to hand back the untouched BufRead; the module tests assert the trailing byte is still readable.

questions.q: I want to hand back the writer with everything pushed out but the compressed stream left open so another one can be appended - is that possible?
questions.why: both encoders have flush_finish(), which calls inner.flush() then take_inner() instead of finish(), and the doc notes you must append 0x3 0x0 yourself to close it.

questions.q: why does the writer adaptor spin in a loop instead of just handing back a zero-length write?
questions.why: write_with_status loops with a comment that the codec may consume nothing and a spurious Ok(0) would break write_all.

questions.q: if I forget to call finish and just let the value go out of scope, is the output still valid?
questions.why: zio::Writer's Drop calls self.finish() when the object is still present, and gz write::GzEncoder's Drop calls try_finish so the trailer is emitted.

questions.q: I hashed two halves of a file separately - can I merge the running sums, and what happens to the byte tally past 4GB?
questions.why: both Crc impls (crc32fast and zlib-rs) expose combine() plus wrapping_add on the amount counter, with the doc noting amount() is only accurate below 2^32.

questions.q: what message do I get back when the bytes turn out not to be a valid stream, and is the backend's own text preserved?
questions.why: zio's read and write_with_status collapse any Err into io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput "corrupt deflate stream"; mem.rs holds the richer CompressError/DecompressError with message().

questions.q: how do I fill a buffer's unused capacity directly and skip zeroing it first?
questions.why: compress_vec/decompress_vec go through the unsafe write_to_spare_capacity_of_vec helper over spare_capacity_mut with MaybeUninit; ffi/mod.rs has the initialize_buffer default used by backends without a native uninit path.

questions.q: I have a shared vocabulary of common strings I want primed before compressing - how do I feed that in, and how do I detect that the other side needs it?
questions.why: Compress/Decompress::set_dictionary (cfg-gated per backend) return the Adler-32, and DecompressError::needs_dictionary reports the NeedsDictionary variant's checksum.

questions.q: can I switch to a cheaper setting partway through without throwing away the object?
questions.why: Compress::set_level (feature any_zlib) either calls deflateParams on the C stream or delegates to the zlib-rs Deflate::set_level, which maps BufError to a failure.

questions.q: with several backend features switched on at once, which one actually gets compiled in, and how does raw vs wrapped output reach the C library?
questions.why: ffi/mod.rs cfg-cascades c -> zlib_rs -> miniz_oxide behind any_c_zlib/any_zlib; ffi/c.rs passes window_bits negated when zlib_header is false to mz_inflateInit2/mz_deflateInit2.

questions.q: how big is the scratch buffer the Read-based wrappers keep, and does a huge read still go through it?
questions.why: the internal BufReader allocates vec![0; 32 * 1024] and its read() bypasses the buffer entirely when pos == cap and the target slice is at least as large; zlib::read::ZlibDecoder::new_with_buf lets you supply that Vec yourself.
